newsitem.title: USA: W.House wants consistency in EU decision on Boeing.
newsitem.headline: W.House wants consistency in EU decision on Boeing.

text.p: The White House wants European Union officials to be consistent when considering the proposed merger of Boeing Co and McDonnell Douglas Corp, spokesman Mike McCurry said on Wednesday.
"We think the principles of competitiveness are those that ought to attend to the European Union's consideration of the proposed merger," McCurry said at his regular briefing.
"We hope it will be done consistently with anti-trust law as it's applied within the (European) Union," he said.
He also said the U.S. government had been in ongoing consultation with EU authorities over the last 48 to 72 hours.
An EU source said earlier Wednesday that EU antitrust experts had agreed that concessions made by Boeing were not enough to win approval for its merger with McDonnell.
Nevertheless, the competition officials asked the European Union executive to explore possibilities for further talks.

Separately, French President Jacques Chirac said France strongly supported the European Commission stance on the merger. "...it could be extremely dangerous for Europeans," Chirac said while on an official visit to Belgium.
